question: How many countries does the Danube River flow through or along on its course from Germany to the Black Sea?
explainer: The Danube passes through or borders Germany, Austria, Slovakia, Hungary, Croatia, Serbia, Bulgaria, Romania, Moldova and Ukraine: more countries than any other river on Earth.

question: How many earthquakes of magnitude 7.0 or greater were recorded worldwide in 2023?
source_title: Earthquake Lists, Maps, and Statistics - USGS
explainer: USGS counts about 15 magnitude-7 quakes in a typical year, so 2023's 19 was a little above average. The February Turkey-Syria doublet (M7.8 and M7.5) made it a deadly year, with roughly 60,000 deaths.

question: How long is the Panama Canal from its Atlantic entrance to its Pacific entrance?
explainer: At 82 km the canal is only about two marathons long, yet a ship transit takes 8 to 10 hours because of the locks and the crossing of Gatun Lake.

question: What was the fastest wind gust ever measured by an anemometer at Earth's surface (Barrow Island, Australia, 1996)?
source_title: Fastest wind speed (recorded by an anemometer) - Guinness World Records
explainer: Tropical Cyclone Olivia produced a 3-second gust of 408 km/h (113 m/s) on 10 April 1996, ratified by the WMO in 2010. That is faster than a Formula 1 car at full speed.

question: How many metres below sea level is the surface of the Dead Sea, as of 2025?
explainer: The Dead Sea's shores are the lowest land on Earth, and the lake is still dropping by more than a metre a year as the Jordan River's inflow is diverted upstream.

question: How tall is Angel Falls in Venezuela, the world's tallest waterfall, from top to bottom?
explainer: At 979 m, Angel Falls is nearly three times the height of the Eiffel Tower, with an uninterrupted plunge of 807 m before the water hits the rocks below.

question: How deep is Lake Baikal in Siberia at its deepest point?
explainer: Baikal is the deepest lake on Earth and holds about one fifth of the world's unfrozen fresh surface water. Four Eiffel Towers stacked in it would still be 300 m short of the surface.

question: How fast is a point on the equator moving because of Earth's rotation alone (ignoring its orbit)?
explainer: Earth's 40,075 km equatorial circumference divided by one sidereal day (23.93 h) gives about 1,674 km/h, faster than the speed of sound at sea level.

question: How many tornadoes were confirmed in the United States in 2023?
explainer: The US averages roughly 1,200 tornadoes a year, more than any other country. A single outbreak on 31 March to 1 April 2023 produced well over 100 of them across the Midwest and South.

question: How long is Australia's Great Barrier Reef, end to end along the Queensland coast?
explainer: Made up of around 3,000 individual reefs and 900 islands, the Great Barrier Reef is roughly the length of the entire west coast of the contiguous United States.

question: How long is the Nile River from its most distant headwater to the Mediterranean Sea?
explainer: At 6,650 km the Nile is about 1,000 km longer than the flight from London to New York. Its exact length is debated, and rival measurements favour the Amazon as the longest river.

question: How many islands make up the Philippines, according to the official NAMRIA count?
source_title: List of islands of the Philippines - Wikipedia
explainer: Satellite mapping lifted the long-standing figure of 7,107 to 7,641. Only about 2,000 of the islands are inhabited and more than 5,000 still have no official name.

question: How deep is the Challenger Deep, the deepest point of the Mariana Trench?
explainer: If Mount Everest were dropped into the Challenger Deep, its summit would still be more than 2 km underwater.

question: How much rain falls in an average year at Mawsynram, India, the wettest inhabited place on Earth?
explainer: Nearly 12 metres of rain a year is about 20 times what London gets. Most of it falls in the monsoon months of June to September.

question: What is the total area of Greenland, the world's largest island?
explainer: Greenland is about three times the size of Texas, but roughly 80% of it is buried under an ice sheet up to 3 km thick.

question: How much water does the Amazon River discharge into the Atlantic every second, on average?
explainer: The Amazon carries about 20% of all the river water that reaches the world's oceans, and more than the next seven largest rivers combined.

question: How many islands does Sweden have, by Statistics Sweden's official 2013 count?
source_title: List of islands of Sweden - Wikipedia
explainer: Sweden has more islands than any other country, though only about 1,000 are inhabited. Norway (239,057) and Finland (178,947) are next on the list.

question: What is the area of the Sahara Desert?
explainer: The Sahara covers about 30% of Africa and is nearly the size of the United States or China. Only Antarctica and the Arctic are larger deserts.

question: What is the surface area of the Pacific Ocean?
explainer: The Pacific covers about 46% of Earth's water surface and nearly a third of the whole planet, more than all of Earth's land area combined.

question: What is the total volume of water in all of Earth's oceans?
source_title: How much water is in the ocean? - NOAA National Ocean Service
explainer: About 1.335 billion cubic kilometres, or 97% of all water on Earth. Spread evenly over the whole globe it would form a layer around 2.6 km deep.

question: How old is the Acasta Gneiss in Canada, one of the oldest known rock formations on Earth?
explainer: At 4.03 billion years, this outcrop in Canada's Northwest Territories formed when Earth was barely 500 million years old. Only a few zircon crystals are older.

question: How much damage did Hurricane Katrina cause in 2005, in 2005 dollars (NOAA estimate)?
explainer: Katrina remains the costliest hurricane in US history; adjusted for inflation the bill is over US$200 billion. Hurricane Harvey in 2017 came closest.

question: What is the total volume of planet Earth?
explainer: Using 4/3 x pi x r³ with Earth's mean radius of 6,371 km gets you to about 1.08 trillion km³. The oceans account for only around 0.1% of that.

question: What is the total mass of Earth's atmosphere?
explainer: Sea-level pressure means about 10 tonnes of air press down on every square metre; multiply by Earth's 510 million km² surface and you get roughly 5 quadrillion tonnes, a millionth of Earth's mass.
